7791.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM6444 : Genomics and Proteomics { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1- Analysis of proteome (6 hours)
Introduction and scope of proteomics and genomics, Protein separation techniques, Isoelectric focusing (IEF), Two dimensional PAGE for proteome analysis, Image analysis of 2D gels, Introduction to mass spectrometry
Module 2- Protein identification strategies (5 hours)
Strategies for protein identification, peptide mass fingerprinting, Protein sequencing, Post translational modifications of proteins, Quantitative proteomics
Module 3- Applications of proteomics (5 hours)
Applications of proteome analysis to drugs, Protein-protein interaction (Two hybrid interaction screening), Protein chips and functional proteomics, Clinical and biomedical application of proteomics, Proteome database and data analysis
Module 4- Analysis of genome (7 hours)
Methods of preparing genomic DNA, DNA sequence analysis methods: Sanger Dideoxy method and Fluorescence method Gene variation and Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs)
Module 5- Applications of genomics (7 hours)
Expressed sequenced tags (ESTs) Gene-disease association, Recombinant DNA technology: DNA cloning basics, Polymerase chain reaction, DNA fingerprinting, Human genome project and the genetic map, CRISPR-Cas9

Course Objective

1 .

Inferring the basic concepts of genomics and proteomics.
2 .

Listing and discussing the use of genomics and proteomics in human health.
3 .

Suggesting and outlining solution to theoretical and experimental problems in Genomics and Proteomics fields.

Course Outcome

1 .

1) To understand various methods of analysis of proteome and genome.
2) To interpret data obtained through high throughput expression studies.
3) To learn different applications of proteomics and genomics in biotechnology and biomedical engineering.
4) To apply basic knowledge of genomics and proteomics to solve theoretical and experimental problems in biotechnology and biomedical engineering.

Essential Reading

1 .

R.M.Twyman, Principles of Proteomics, BIOS Scientific Publishers, 2004.

2 .

Arthur M Lesk, Introduction to Genomics, Oxford University Press, 2007.

Supplementary Reading

1 .

P. Michael Conn, Handbook of Proteomic Method, Humana Press, Totowa, New Jersay, USA, 2003.

2 .

L. Stryer, Biochemistry, W. H. Freeman and Co., New York, 2007.

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : ER5673 : Satellite Meteorology and Oceanography Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Understanding the variability of meteorological and oceanographic parameters from different satellites. The satellites include INSTAT series, KALPANA, AQUA, TERRA, LANDSAT, IRS series, QuikSCAT, SCATSAT, OCEANSAT, METSAT, CHANDRAYAN satellites, Mars bound satellites etc. The parameters include, SST, TCHP, AOD, AE, WIND, TEMPERATURE, LU, RAINFALL etc...The software to be adopted are GrADS, MATLAB, NCL, NetCDF, HDF, CDO etc.

To familiarize the students about different meteorological and ocean parameters retrieved from different satellites, how to handle the data sets and plot them using the available software and how to analyze their variability.

1 .

The students would gain practical knowledge about satellite meteorology and oceanography applications.

5999.t: HS5423: Contemporary Policy Issues in Development
5999.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : HS5423 : Contemporary Policy Issues in Development { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Modules:
Unit 1: Structure of Indian Economy
Indian Economy in the Pre-British Period, Trend and Pattern of Economic Development after Independence: Population growth and development, National Income, Poverty and Inequality, Human Resources and Development: Health and Education, Occupational Structure, Natural Resources, Infrastructure
Unit 2: Planning and Economic Development
Economic Planning – Types of Planning, Goal and Strategies of Indian Planning, Market Mechanism and State Intervention, Public Sector and Disinvestment Policy, Economic Reforms and Liberalisation, The role of NITI Aayog
Unit 3: Agriculture, Industry and Development
Indian Agriculture since Independence, Food Security in India, Irrigation and other agricultural inputs, Land reforms, Size of farm and productive efficiencies, Rural Credit and Agricultural Marketing, Indian Agricultural Policies, Industrial Pattern Large – Medium - Small – Micro Enterprises Unorganized Sector and Informalization of Indian Economy Indian Industrial Policies
Unit 4: Trade Policy and Development
Foreign Trade of India India’s Balance of Payments Special Economic Zone (SEZ) GATT, WTO and India’s Foreign Trade, Indian Currency and Financial System, Indian Trade Policies
Unit 5: Health, Nutrition and Education
Health and nutrition divide in India, contemporary health and nutrition policies and human development, Fiscal space for health, nutrition and education, new education policy

Course Objective

1 .

• To study the major challenges and opportunities in the major sectors of the Indian Economy like Agriculture, Industry and foreign sectors.

Course Outcome

1 .

On successful completion of the course, students will be able to:
1. Learn the basic features of Indian economy and also understand the practices and policies related to Indian economic development.
2. Examine major challenges and opportunities in the key sectors of the Indian Economy like Agriculture and Industry.
3. Gain knowledge of how trade policies and financial systems affect India’s economic development
4. Know policies related to education, health and nutrition from public policy perspectives.
5. Analyse the impact of sectoral plans on economic development in India.

Essential Reading

1 .

Misra, S.K. and V.K. Puri, Indian Economy — Its Development Experience, Himalaya Publishing House, Mumbai. , (71st Revised Edition, 2015)

2 .

Bhahmananda, P.R. and V.R. Panchmukhi, The Development Process of the Indian Economy, Himalaya Publishing House, Bombay

Supplementary Reading

Kapila, U.,, Indian Economy since Independence, Academic Foundation, New Delhi. 2014.

2 .

Datt, R. and K.P.M. Sundharam ,, Indian Economy, S. Chand & Co Ltd., New Delhi. 2015

6255.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : MN6004 : Material Handling System { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Total contact hours = 30-37
Module 1: Material handling methods in mining industries. Aerial Ropeway: Monocable, bi-cable, twin-cable ropeway, constructional features and power calculations, selection and application.
[5-7 classes]
Module 2: Mine hoist: Drum and koepe winders, constructional features, kinematics, torque and power calculation, speed control, safety contrivances, selection of mine winders, cages, skip, suspension gears, headgear structures, cage guides, pit top and pit bottom circuits and layouts. [10-11 classes]
Module 3: Conveyors: Belt conveyor, High angle conveyors, chain conveyor, cable belt conveyor, shaker conveyor, vibratory conveyor, constructional features and power calculations, selection and application. [4-5 classes]
Module 4: Pipeline transport, Scraper Haulage: Constructional features, applicability, advantages and disadvantages. [3-4 classes]
Module 5: Men and material transportation: Cutting and loading machines for coal/ore, special men and materials transport in mines, men riding systems in mines. [8-10 classes]

Course Objective

1 .

To familiarize students with men and material handling methods and its applications in mining industries.
2 .

To equip students with advanced knowledge of aerial ropeway, shaft hoisting, conveyors, pipeline transport, cutting and loading machines, men & material transport systems in mines.
3 .

To develop skills in designing, analyzing and optimizing the use of material transport systems.

Course Outcome

1 .

1. To understand the concept and applications of men & material handling systems in mining industries.
2. To estimate the performance of the aerial ropeway, shaft hoisting system and conveyors in mines.
3. To design aerial ropeway, shaft hoisting system, pit-top & pit-bottom layout, conveyors, special men & material transport system for mines.
4. To know the advanced system for men & material transport for short and long-haul distance in mining industries.
5. To identify the importance of cutting and loading machines used in underground mines with material transportation in mines.

Essential Reading

1 .

D. J. Deshmukh, Elements of mining technology, Vol. 3, Denett & Co., Nagpur

2 .

N. Mukherjee, Materials handling in mines, Vol- XI, Technology mining society IIT Kharagpur , 1st Ed

Supplementary Reading

1 .

M. P. Alexandrov, Material handling equipment, MIR , 1st Ed

2 .

Peter Darling, SME Mining Engineering Handbook, Vol. 1, Society for Mining, Metallurgy, and Exploration Inc. (US) , 3rd Ed

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : SM6322 : Organization Change and Development { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Organizational Change: Forces of Organizational Change, Need for Change and Innovation, Resistance to Change, Organizational Change Process, Organizational Diagnosis. Change Agents: Role of Change Agents, Competency Requirements, Training of Change Agents, Effective Change Leader, Executing Organizational Change.
Organization Development (OD): Foundations of OD, OD Process, Six-Box Model, Evaluating OD Effectiveness, Factors Influencing OD. OD Interventions: Individual and Interpersonal Interventions, Group Interventions, Role Focused Interventions, Third Party and Structural Intervention, Role of Organizational Leadership. Contemporary Issues and Applications: OD Practitioners, Success and Failure of OD, Organizational Transformation, OD in Global Context, Future Trends in OD.

Course Objective

1 .

The objective is to study the influence of change management and how it affects organizations and the individuals within those organizations. It also provide an in-depth knowledge of the strategies that can be developed to introduce planned change, such as team-building efforts, to improve organizational functioning.

Course Outcome

1 .

This course is designed to provide in depth understanding of behavioural interventions and enable the students to apply these interventions for building individual, team, systems and process related competencies.

Essential Reading

1 .

Cummings, T. G., & Worley, C. G. (2014), Theory of Organization Development and Change (9thed.), Cengage Learning

2 .

Jones, G. R. (2012)., Organizational Theory, Design and Change (7thed.)., Pearson Education

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Palmer, I., Dunford, R., & Akin, G. (2005)., Managing Organizational Change., Tata McGraw Hill Education.

2 .

Singh, K. (2009)., Organization Change and Development, Excel Books.
